questions.title: Harden the dashboard
questions.text:
The Kubernetes Dashboard in namespace `kubernetes-dashboard` is exposed on a NodePort and started with insecure options.

Change the Service `kubernetes-dashboard` to type `ClusterIP`, and remove the arguments `--enable-skip-login` and `--enable-insecure-login` from the Deployment `kubernetes-dashboard`. Keep the other arguments. The Deployment must stay available.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n kubernetes-dashboard get svc,deploy
    kubectl -n kubernetes-dashboard patch svc kubernetes-dashboard -p '{"spec":{"type":"ClusterIP"}}'
    kubectl -n kubernetes-dashboard edit deployment kubernetes-dashboard   # delete the two args
    kubectl -n kubernetes-dashboard rollout status deployment kubernetes-dashboard

When patching a NodePort service to ClusterIP, also clear the `nodePort` fields in `spec.ports` if the API complains. Reach the dashboard afterwards through `kubectl proxy` or `kubectl port-forward`, never a NodePort.

references.title: Deploy and Access the Kubernetes Dashboard

checks.name: kubernetes-dashboard
checks.hint: the dashboard deployment is not available

questions.title: DNS and CIDR-only egress
questions.text:
The Pod `proxy` (label `app=proxy`) in namespace `edge` must only be able to send traffic to:

- DNS in namespace `kube-system` (TCP and UDP port `53`)
- the external range `10.10.0.0/16`

Create a NetworkPolicy `proxy-egress` in `edge` that allows exactly that. Afterwards `proxy` must **not** be able to reach the `api` pods in its own namespace.
questions.solution:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: NetworkPolicy
    metadata:
      name: proxy-egress
      namespace: edge
    spec:
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: proxy
      policyTypes:
      - Egress
      egress:
      - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
        ports:
        - protocol: UDP
          port: 53
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 53
      - to:
        - ipBlock:
            cidr: 10.10.0.0/16

Pod IPs live in `10.244.0.0/16`, so the `10.10.0.0/16` block does not cover in-cluster pods — which is exactly why `proxy` loses access to `api`. Verify: `kubectl -n edge exec proxy -- wget -qO- --timeout=2 api` times out.

checks.name: proxy-egress
checks.hint: proxy-egress must select app=proxy, be an Egress policy and allow ipBlock 10.10.0.0/16

checks.name: proxy-egress
checks.hint: proxy-egress must allow port 53 to namespace kube-system
proxy must no longer reach the api pods

questions.title: CIS findings for the control plane
questions.text:
Run `kube-bench` on `cks3-control` and remediate these findings:

- `1.2.19` — the API server must set `--audit-log-maxsize=100`
- `1.3.6` — the controller manager must enable `RotateKubeletServerCertificate` via `--feature-gates=RotateKubeletServerCertificate=true`

Both components must stay healthy.
questions.solution:
ssh cks3-control
    sudo -i
    kube-bench
    vim /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml            # add: - --audit-log-maxsize=100
    vim /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-controller-manager.yaml   # add: - --feature-gates=RotateKubeletServerCertificate=true
    kube-bench --check 1.2.19,1.3.6
    exit; exit

(kube-bench also reports 1.2.6/1.2.14 about admission plugins — that is the next task.)

questions.title: API server admission and TLS
questions.text:
On `cks3-control` the API server currently enables the `AlwaysAdmit` admission plugin.

Change the manifest so that the enabled admission plugins are `NodeRestriction` (and **not** `AlwaysAdmit`), and require TLS 1.2 or newer with `--tls-min-version=VersionTLS12`. The API server must come back healthy.
questions.solution:
ssh cks3-control
    sudo -i
    vim /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml
      # - --enable-admission-plugins=AlwaysAdmit   ->   - --enable-admission-plugins=NodeRestriction
      # add:  - --tls-min-version=VersionTLS12
    exit; exit
    kubectl get nodes

`NodeRestriction` stops a compromised kubelet from modifying other nodes' objects; `AlwaysAdmit` disables admission control altogether and is removed in current Kubernetes releases.

checks.hint: kube-apiserver must enable the NodeRestriction admission plugin
AlwaysAdmit must be removed from the admission plugins

questions.title: Clean up service accounts
questions.text:
In namespace `ci`:

- the `default` ServiceAccount must not auto-mount API tokens (`automountServiceAccountToken: false`)
- the unused ServiceAccount `legacy-deploy` and its RoleBinding `legacy-deploy-rb` must be deleted (keep the Role `deployer`)
questions.solution:
kubectl -n ci patch serviceaccount default -p '{"automountServiceAccountToken": false}'
    kubectl -n ci get rolebindings -o wide
    kubectl -n ci delete rolebinding legacy-deploy-rb
    kubectl -n ci delete serviceaccount legacy-deploy

Every pod without an explicit `serviceAccountName` uses `default`; disabling its token mount means a compromised pod finds no credentials at `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount`.

checks.name: default
checks.hint: the default serviceaccount in ci must set automountServiceAccountToken: false

questions.title: Read-only Secret access for a group
questions.text:
Members of the group `security-auditors` need to read Secrets in every namespace, and nothing more.

Create a ClusterRole `secret-reader` allowing `get` and `list` on `secrets`, and a ClusterRoleBinding `auditors-secrets` that grants it to the group.
questions.solution:
kubectl create clusterrole secret-reader --verb=get,list --resource=secrets
    kubectl create clusterrolebinding auditors-secrets --clusterrole=secret-reader --group=security-auditors
    kubectl auth can-i list secrets --as=someone --as-group=security-auditors   # yes
    kubectl auth can-i delete secrets --as=someone --as-group=security-auditors # no

Groups come from the authenticator (certificate O= fields, OIDC claims); binding to a group avoids editing RBAC every time a person joins or leaves.

checks.name: auditors-secrets
checks.hint: clusterrolebinding auditors-secrets must bind secret-reader to group security-auditors
security-auditors must be able to list secrets
security-auditors must not be able to delete secrets

questions.title: AppArmor for a Deployment
questions.text:
An AppArmor profile `k8s-restricted` is available as a file at `/etc/apparmor.d/k8s-restricted` on both worker nodes (`cks3-node1`, `cks3-node2`) but is not loaded.

Load it on **both** nodes, then apply it at the **pod level** (`spec.securityContext.appArmorProfile`) to the Deployment `reports` in namespace `edge`. The Deployment must remain available.
questions.solution:
ssh cks3-node1 sudo apparmor_parser -q /etc/apparmor.d/k8s-restricted
    ssh cks3-node2 sudo apparmor_parser -q /etc/apparmor.d/k8s-restricted
    kubectl -n edge edit deployment reports

    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          securityContext:
            appArmorProfile:
              type: Localhost
              localhostProfile: k8s-restricted

    kubectl -n edge rollout status deployment reports

A Deployment can land on any worker, so the profile must be present on every node it might run on; otherwise those pods fail with `AppArmor profile not found`.

checks.hint: profile k8s-restricted is not loaded on cks3-node1
profile k8s-restricted is not loaded on cks3-node2

checks.name: reports
checks.hint: reports pod template must set pod-level appArmorProfile Localhost/k8s-restricted

checks.name: reports
checks.hint: deployment reports is not fully available

questions.title: Kernel hardening with sysctl
questions.text:
On node `cks3-node1`, harden two kernel parameters **persistently** and apply them now:

- `net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0`
- `kernel.dmesg_restrict = 1`

Put the settings in `/etc/sysctl.d/99-hardening.conf`.
questions.solution:
ssh cks3-node1
    sudo -i
    sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects kernel.dmesg_restrict      # current values
    vim /etc/sysctl.d/99-hardening.conf
      # net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0
      # kernel.dmesg_restrict = 1
    sysctl --system            # or: sysctl -p /etc/sysctl.d/99-hardening.conf
    sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects kernel.dmesg_restrict
    exit; exit

`sysctl -w` changes the running kernel only; the file under `/etc/sysctl.d/` is what survives a reboot.

references.title: Using sysctls in a Kubernetes Cluster

checks.hint: the running kernel still accepts ICMP redirects (apply the settings)
kernel.dmesg_restrict is not applied to the running kernel

questions.title: Move a Secret between namespaces
questions.text:
The Secret `db-conn` in namespace `vault` has the keys `user` and `pass`.

1. Write the **decoded** value of `user` to `/opt/answers/db-user.txt` and of `pass` to `/opt/answers/db-pass.txt` on the base host.
2. Create a Secret named `db-conn` in namespace `vault2` with the same two keys and values.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n vault get secret db-conn -o jsonpath='{.data.user}' | base64 -d > /opt/answers/db-user.txt
    kubectl -n vault get secret db-conn -o jsonpath='{.data.pass}' | base64 -d > /opt/answers/db-pass.txt
    kubectl -n vault2 create secret generic db-conn --from-literal=user="$(cat /opt/answers/db-user.txt)" --from-literal=pass="$(cat /opt/answers/db-pass.txt)"

Command substitution `$(...)` is not available in this lab — read the files and type the values instead:

    kubectl -n vault2 create secret generic db-conn --from-literal=user=dbadmin --from-literal='pass=Tr0ub4dor&3'

Quote values containing shell metacharacters. Alternatively export the Secret to YAML, change `metadata.namespace`, strip `uid`/`resourceVersion`, and apply.

checks.name: db-conn
checks.hint: secret db-conn in vault2 must hold the same user and pass values

questions.title: Sandbox a Deployment with gVisor
questions.text: A RuntimeClass `gvisor` exists. Make every pod of the Deployment `untrusted` in namespace `edge` run in the gVisor sandbox. The Deployment must remain available.
questions.solution:
kubectl get runtimeclass
    kubectl -n edge patch deployment untrusted -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"runtimeClassName":"gvisor"}}}}'
    kubectl -n edge rollout status deployment untrusted
    kubectl -n edge get pods -l app=untrusted -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.runtimeClassName}'

gVisor intercepts the container's syscalls in a user-space kernel, so a kernel exploit inside the container does not reach the host.

checks.name: untrusted
checks.hint: untrusted pod template must set runtimeClassName: gvisor

checks.name: untrusted
checks.hint: deployment untrusted is not fully available

questions.title: Restricted namespace with a CronJob
questions.text:
Enforce the `restricted` Pod Security Standard on namespace `ci`. The CronJob `nightly` there would be rejected under that standard.

Apply the label and fix the CronJob's pod template so that its jobs will be admitted: no privileged container, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped, non-root, and the `RuntimeDefault` seccomp profile.
questions.solution:
kubectl label namespace ci pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted
    kubectl -n ci edit cronjob nightly

    jobTemplate:
      spec:
        template:
          spec:
            containers:
            - name: main
              image: busybox:1.36
              command: ["sh", "-c", "echo nightly"]
              securityContext:
                allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                runAsNonRoot: true
                capabilities:
                  drop: ["ALL"]
                seccompProfile:
                  type: RuntimeDefault

Test with a one-off run: `kubectl -n ci create job --from=cronjob/nightly test-run` — its pod is admitted only if the template complies.

checks.name: nightly
checks.hint: nightly's container must be non-privileged, allowPrivilegeEscalation false, drop ALL, runAsNonRoot true, seccomp RuntimeDefault

questions.title: ImagePolicyWebhook
questions.text:
An image policy webhook has been prepared on `cks3-control` under `/etc/kubernetes/admission/` (admission configuration, kubeconfig and certificates).

Finish the setup:

- in `admission-config.yaml` set `defaultAllow` to `false` so images are **denied** when the webhook is unreachable
- enable the `ImagePolicyWebhook` admission plugin on the API server (keep `NodeRestriction`) and point it at the configuration with `--admission-control-config-file=/etc/kubernetes/admission/admission-config.yaml`

The API server must come back healthy.
questions.solution:
ssh cks3-control
    sudo -i
    ls /etc/kubernetes/admission/
    vim /etc/kubernetes/admission/admission-config.yaml     # defaultAllow: false
    vim /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml
      # - --enable-admission-plugins=NodeRestriction,ImagePolicyWebhook
      # - --admission-control-config-file=/etc/kubernetes/admission/admission-config.yaml
      # and mount /etc/kubernetes/admission into the container (hostPath + volumeMount, readOnly)
    exit; exit
    kubectl get nodes

`defaultAllow: true` is fail-open: any webhook outage lets every image through. The kubeconfig inside the admission configuration is what tells the API server where the webhook lives and how to authenticate to it.

checks.hint: kube-apiserver must enable the ImagePolicyWebhook admission plugin

questions.title: Static analysis triage
questions.text:
The directory `~/manifests/` on the base host holds four manifests (`a.yaml` … `d.yaml`) for namespace `tools`.

Analyse each with `kubesec scan`. Apply **only** the manifests with no critical findings; do not apply the others.
questions.solution:
for f in ~/manifests/*.yaml; do echo $f; kubesec scan $f | grep -E '"message"|"id": "(Privileged|HostNetwork|HostPID)"'; done
    # loops are not simulated here: run kubesec scan on each file
    kubesec scan ~/manifests/a.yaml    # Passed
    kubesec scan ~/manifests/b.yaml    # Failed: Privileged
    kubesec scan ~/manifests/c.yaml    # Passed
    kubesec scan ~/manifests/d.yaml    # Failed: HostNetwork, HostPID
    kubectl apply -f ~/manifests/a.yaml
    kubectl apply -f ~/manifests/c.yaml

A `critical` entry in the scoring makes the manifest fail regardless of the other points; `advise` entries are improvements, not blockers.

checks.name: metrics
checks.hint: a.yaml (pod metrics) has no critical findings and should be applied

checks.name: worker
checks.hint: c.yaml (deployment worker) has no critical findings and should be applied

checks.name: debug
checks.hint: b.yaml (pod debug) is privileged and must not be applied

checks.name: netdiag
checks.hint: d.yaml (pod netdiag) uses host namespaces and must not be applied

questions.title: Always pull images
questions.text: The Deployments `shop` and `blog` in namespace `web` use `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`, so a node's cached image could be used even after the tag was updated in the registry. Set `imagePullPolicy: Always` on their containers. Both must remain available.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n web patch deployment shop -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"main","imagePullPolicy":"Always"}]}}}}'
    kubectl -n web patch deployment blog -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"main","imagePullPolicy":"Always"}]}}}}'
    kubectl -n web rollout status deployment shop
    kubectl -n web rollout status deployment blog

Strategic merge patches match containers by `name`, so this patch changes only the pull policy. The `AlwaysPullImages` admission plugin enforces the same thing cluster-wide.

questions.title: Targeted audit policy
questions.text:
Configure API server auditing on `cks3-control` with a policy at `/etc/kubernetes/audit/policy.yaml` that:

- logs changes to **pods in namespace `prod`** at the `Request` level
- logs **nothing** (`None`) for everything else

Write the log to `/var/log/kubernetes/audit/audit.log` (`--audit-log-path`) and reference the policy with `--audit-log-maxage=7`. The API server must stay healthy.
questions.solution:
ssh cks3-control
    sudo -i
    mkdir -p /etc/kubernetes/audit /var/log/kubernetes/audit
    vim /etc/kubernetes/audit/policy.yaml

    apiVersion: audit.k8s.io/v1
    kind: Policy
    rules:
    - level: Request
      namespaces: ["prod"]
      resources:
      - group: ""
        resources: ["pods"]
    - level: None

    vim /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml
      # - --audit-policy-file=/etc/kubernetes/audit/policy.yaml
      # - --audit-log-path=/var/log/kubernetes/audit/audit.log
      # - --audit-log-maxage=7
      # plus hostPath mounts for both directories
    exit; exit

The first matching rule wins, so the specific `Request` rule must come before the catch-all `None`. A `None` catch-all keeps the log small and the sensitive-data footprint low.

checks.hint: the policy must log at level Request
the Request rule must target pods
the Request rule must be limited to namespace prod
everything else must be level None

questions.title: Falco file output
questions.text: Falco on `cks3-node1` only writes to syslog and stdout. Configure it (`/etc/falco/falco.yaml`) to also write events to the file `/var/log/falco/events.txt` (enable `file_output` with that `filename`), then restart Falco. The service must be running.
questions.solution:
ssh cks3-node1
    sudo -i
    vim /etc/falco/falco.yaml

    file_output:
      enabled: true
      keep_alive: false
      filename: /var/log/falco/events.txt

    systemctl restart falco
    systemctl status falco
    exit; exit

`falco.yaml` has one block per output channel (syslog, file, stdout, http, program); each is switched with `enabled`. Restart the service for the change to take effect.

questions.title: Find the pod that mounts the host
questions.text: One of the pods in namespace `ops` mounts the node's **root filesystem** (`/`) via a `hostPath` volume. Identify it and delete it. Leave the other pods in the namespace running.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n ops get pods -o yaml | grep -B3 -A3 hostPath
    # or: kubectl -n ops get pods -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.spec.volumes[*].hostPath.path}{"\n"}{end}'
    kubectl -n ops delete pod node-tool

A `hostPath` of `/` gives the container the whole node: kubelet credentials, other containers' filesystems, everything. Search for it the same way across all namespaces with `-A`.

checks.name: node-tool
checks.hint: pod node-tool mounts hostPath / and must be deleted
